4) Quædam compofita 5. declin. fimplicium ut κλαωσιγέλως. φιλόγελως ὁ qui facile ridet, qui facetiis delectatur, &c. 5) item alia nonnulla, ut ὀλίγος exiguus, ποικίλ varius, ἀνωτ contrarius, νυμφι sponsus, σκορπι scorpius: omniaq; adjecta. in αλε ut ἡχα-λέ molestus, πνῦχαλέ luctuosus. 6) verbalia in ἱ. vide infra §.103. 7) Diminutiva in ἰσκ, ut ψαωίσκ juvenculus. 8) verbalia in cum nominibus è præt. medio ortis compofita, quæ si actively capiantur, sunt προζύτωνα, ut Actor.17.18. ἀστεμβολόγ nugator, 1.Timoth.1.v.9. ἀνδροφόν homicida, Luc.12.42. οἰκονόμ domus altor, qui pascit seu alit familiam. θεολόγ ὁ qui de Deo differit. Sic κληρονόμ hares, μεγαλάλ, qui vix fari potest.

main_text.l: ἰχθυοφάγος ὁ ἡ qui vel qua pisces edit.
ἰχθυοφάγος ὁ ἡ qui vel qua à pisculbus editur.
main_text.p: Exceptionem nonnulli observant in Pindar. Olymp. Od.6. (p.109.) ubi λαοτρόφ πιμὴ vocatur honor (τεμφόμψ ὑπὸ ὁ λαὸς) nutritus à populo & alicui tributus vel à populo celebratus. Vide Lexicon Porti p.322. Alii tamen active accipiunt & vertunt honorem populi altorem.

page.notes: Right page is a narrow margin column with fragmentary text (marginal notes, partly cut off at the edge, including headings "Acce..." and numbered notes 25, 26, 27, 28, 29 and references such as Act.18.vis., Act.4.a.i., Jacob.4.8., Act.18.3.). Greek and Latin fragments are too damaged to transcribe reliably and are not given here. Lines of the left page at the bottom are partly italic Greek; transcribed as best as possible. Some Greek readings are uncertain.
